_header: Emergency guide V3 (20/11/2026). Every step cites a NASA source read on 20/11/2026; a step without a source is refused by tests/test_emergency_guide.py. C-Sync proposes no treatment and no drug. The station's own alarms and the onboard checklists come first; C-Sync keeps the steps, the clock, the headcount and the report.

sources.TOBIAS2023: Tobias B., McMillan C., Evolution of Hardware and Philosophy of Emergency Response Actions on the ISS, SpaceOps 2023, NASA NTRS 20220019247
sources.TB004: NASA OCHMO-TB-004, Carbon Dioxide technical brief (NASA-STD-3001)
sources.TB037: NASA OCHMO-TB-037, Decompression Sickness Risk Mitigation technical brief
sources.DESIGN: C-Sync design choice (not a NASA procedure)

cases.title: Medical: a crew member reports a symptom (chest pain in the demo)
cases.trigger: A crew member reports a symptom and its body zone.
cases.csync_role: Opens the guided procedure, takes the measurements one by one with their time, queues the report for the ground.

steps.text: Stop the current task and alert the crew.
Mark the body zone where the symptom is felt.
Take the measurements one at a time on the onboard devices (heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, glucose); C-Sync records each value with its time.
Follow the onboard medical checklist and the crew medical officer.
The report is built from the recorded values only and queued for the ground; it is delivered once when the link returns.

cases.never: C-Sync never interprets the symptom and never proposes a treatment or a drug.

cases.title: Rapid depressurization (air leak)
cases.trigger: Cabin pressure falling: station alarm, or C-Sync sees the pressure drop on two readings.
cases.csync_role: Computes the time left before the cabin reaches 490 mmHg from two pressure readings, and keeps the headcount.

steps.text: Warn: the station alarm sounds; anyone can also trigger it.
Gather: everyone meets at the designated point and is counted.
Compute the time left before cabin pressure reaches 490 mmHg (9.5 psia) from a gauge and a timer.
Check that the return vehicle is leak-tight before anything else.
Close hatches to isolate modules until the leak is found. Never close a hatch between the crew and the return vehicle.
When ten minutes or less remain: stop isolating and retreat to the safe haven.
Afterwards, report any joint pain, tingling, numbness, skin rash, weakness, confusion or balance trouble to the crew medical officer (decompression sickness signs).

cases.never: C-Sync does not command hatches or valves; it computes and records.

cases.title: Fire or smoke
cases.trigger: Station smoke alarm or crew report.
cases.csync_role: Keeps the headcount, the clock of each step and the log; the station removes power and fans on its own.

steps.text: Warn and gather: confirm a safe haven and account for everyone.
Put on breathing masks to leave the area; switch to respirators with fire cartridges once in the safe haven.
Locate the source with station telemetry and air samples.
Remove power from the equipment behind the panel.
Use the extinguisher the onboard procedure names for that location.
If the fire persists: power down the module and leave it.
After the fire: the air is scrubbed before the crew returns.

cases.never: C-Sync does not judge whether the fire is out; the crew decides.

cases.title: Toxic leak (ammonia)
cases.trigger: Station alarm or crew report of a smell or leak.
cases.csync_role: Shows the memorized response in order, keeps the headcount and the log.

steps.text: Put on protective masks.
Leave the contaminated segment for the safe segment or the return vehicle.
Close the hatches to isolate the contaminated segment.
Switch to filtering respirators as the procedure says.

cases.never: C-Sync does not decide when the air is safe again.

cases.title: Cabin CO2 too high
cases.trigger: CO2 above NASA's 3 mmHg one-hour limit (C-Sync reads it live) or crew headaches.
cases.csync_role: Cross-checks two cabin sensors, records who reports symptoms, and alerts once per episode.

steps.text: Check that the reading is real: compare two cabin sensors before alerting.
Alert the crew and the ground: NASA limits the one-hour average to 3 mmHg.
Each crew member reports headache, fatigue, poor sleep or nausea; C-Sync records who and when.
The ground and crew adjust the air system by their own procedure; C-Sync follows the value until it is back under the limit.

cases.never: C-Sync does not change the air system.
